gates.question: Publishing to the public home keeps each commit's author and committer byte for byte (kbpublic.py, projection); on 2026-10-19 the last 3000 commits of the main branch had a personal-mail author in 2727 and a noreply one in 273. Should publish change how it treats these emails?
options: keep the published history as it is; publish warns on each new commit whose author or committer email is no noreply or placeholder one
publish refuses such a commit until its author is a noreply address
the projection rewrites author and committer emails to a noreply address, a one-time rewrite of the public home's history
gates.recommendation: keep the published history as it is; publish warns on each new commit whose author or committer email is no noreply or placeholder one

notes: Premise (2026-10-19): a planted publish --dry-run of a commit authored with a non-placeholder address prints no warning. Waits on the operator's gate g-author (class push); the check fits the recommended answer, and another answer rewords it before the claim. Test policy (D-6kei5o2z, D-2tq4fhgs): no new test or test file; the check is a tool run on a throwaway clone built from this checkout's _tools and .claude/hooks with its own coord store and a stub claude on PATH; no change to _tools/tests_ceiling.json. Design: kb/_self/design.md, Teams and organizations; facts: public/claude/ci-and-headless.md:124-127, public/claude/otel-monitoring.md:51-53, QK-claude-code-session-learn-email-account.
